lysolipid-containing liposomes exhibit a significant permeability increase at temperatures two degrees below their phase transition temperature and extend for several degrees above it.
lysolipid temperature sensitive liposomes (LTLS) are capable of releasing their contents at temperatures that can be easily achieved in the clinic.

the lysolipids in LTSLs remain stable in the membrane and create long-lasting pores that allow for enhanced permeability and drug diffusion at temperatures below the phase transition temperature of the liposomes.

the lysolipids in these liposomes act as a stabilizing agent for the grain boundaries of the liposome bilayer, and that when heated, the lysolipds desorb from the bilayer, leaving the grain boundaries permeable to molecules and drugs.

we have developed a temperature triggered drug release system that can deliver drugs to a tumor at a temperature of about 40 °C, which can be achieved with a focused ultrasound beam.

the temperature-triggered nanotechnology is based on the fact that the liposomes are stable at room temperature and release their drug contents at the tumor site, which is heated by the hyperthermia treatment.

lysolipid-containing liposomes are a viable and effective method of temperature-sensitive drug delivery, and can be used to enhance permeability in membranes.
